title: Cross-tenant quota multiplexing leak and rate-smoothing playbook
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

During a traffic surge on 2026-02-12 we observed a sustained wave of 429s affecting multiple tenants. Root cause analysis shows an auth token multiplexing optimization introduced in gateway-2.12 combined with a subtle permutation in quota key generation. Under high parallelism the gateway reused a shared multiplexed token context which caused quota attribution to collapse to a small set of derived tenant keys. The effect: per-tenant rate windows were artificially merged causing fast exhaustion of shared quota buckets and large numbers of 429s for tenants that were not the traffic originators.

Why this happened (technical):
- An optimization (PR #GH-3265) that pooled token verification contexts to reduce crypto handshakes created a reused context object when requests shared identical header fingerprints.
- Quota key generation relied on a two-part key: tenant_id + context_hash. The pooling produced identical context_hash across distinct tenant sessions during bursts, producing cross-tenant key collisions.
- The collision surface increased with the introduction of a new deterministic canonicalization of headers in the same PR; previously entropy in ordering implicitly reduced collision rate.
- Rate smoothing logic (newly enabled by feature-flag) did not account for collisions and accelerated refill/consume decisions in a way that amplified the throttling cascade.

Immediate mitigation applied (Feb 12-13):
- Hotfix GH-PR-3321 reverted the pooling behavior for contexts in the auth path and rolled back the deterministic header canonicalization. Deployed as hot-patch to regional gateways (us-west-2, eu-central-1) at 2026-02-12 21:37 UTC.
- Emergency rule added in the quota enforcer to detect unusually high share of requests mapping to same quota key and to temporarily split attribution (soft split) to avoid hard collisions.
- Increased quota reporting frequency to enable faster detection for SRE dashboards.

Follow-up analysis and constraints:
- The root design issue is relying on derived hash values from mutable/pooled objects for core tenant isolation guarantees.
- Rate smoothing is beneficial, but the smoothing algorithm must be collision-aware and use stable, collision-resistant tenant identifiers.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident timeline and raw spans: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-12+Gateway+429+wave
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/3321
- Root-cause revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/3340
- Metric dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/txn/gateway-429-wave

Decision log (engineering + PM):
- We will not reintroduce context pooling until a collision-proof keying scheme is validated (decision 2026-02-20).
- Rate smoothing will be disabled by default for tenants above X RPS until we've added collision detection and fallback logic (decision 2026-02-21).

Longer-term proposals (evaluated):
- Use HKDF-based tenant binding for quota keys (salted per-instance KMS value) to eliminate deterministic collisions across pooled contexts.
- Introduce per-tenant monotonic nonces surfaced from the auth service so quota keys do not depend on request header ordering/canonicalization.
- Add a probabilistic monitoring probe that intentionally introduces micro-variance to improve key entropy in edge cases (experimental).

Expected outcome:
- Restore tenant isolation for quota enforcement and reduce risk of cross-tenant throttling cascades.
- Provide an operational playbook so SREs can detect and neutralize similar edge cases quickly without a full rollback.

2026-02-12 19:29 UTC - SRE page and incident channel created, initial triage points to quota enforcer
2026-02-12 20:05 UTC - Correlation found between high key collision metric and tenant 0x8d9e
2026-02-12 21:37 UTC - Hotfix GH-PR-3321 deployed to us-west-2 and eu-central-1
2026-02-13 02:10 UTC - 429 rates dropped to baseline in hotfixed regions; global rollout initiated
2026-02-15 14:00 UTC - Post-incident RCA meeting with PMs, design and SRE; agreed on playbook items

updates: 2026-02-16 - Preliminary RCA draft circulated; requested additional telemetry for header canonicalization statistics (assigned to Eng-Metrics)
2026-02-22 - Security flagged that HKDF-based tenant binding requires KMS change; added security review to the dependencies
2026-03-01 - Benchmarked HKDF option; CPU cost acceptable at scale (notes in GH-branch hkdf-keying)
2026-03-08 - Completed integration test that simulates high-parallelism header permutations; no collisions observed after HKDF keying applied
action_items: A1: Replace pooled-context-based context_hash with HKDF-salted tenant binding for quota keys. Owner: Diego Morales. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-20. PR: GH-PR-3512
A2: Add collision detector metric and alert rule (SRE). Owner: Priya Menon. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-05. Dashboard panel: gateway.quota.collision_rate
A3: Update rate-smoothing algorithm to check for key-entropy score before applying aggressive smoothing; fallback to conservative path on low entropy. Owner: Martin Hall. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-18

A4: Create operator runbook steps for detecting and performing a soft-split mitigation without rollback. Owner: Oncall SRE lead. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-03. Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Gateway+Quota+Playbook
A5: Security review for HKDF KMS integration and key lifecycle. Owner: Security Team (Ana Rivera). Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-12
A6: Canary rollout schedule across regions with traffic mirroring and gradual enablement flag. Owner: Diego Morales. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-20
